newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post Front Page - Oct 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post Front Page - Oct 23.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Oct 23:

DETROIT - President Clinton turned his campaign to foreign policy, offering a broad defense of his handling of global affairs and making a specific pledge that NATO will accept its first former Warsaw Pact members by 1999.
WASHINGTON - Federal prosecutors charged a former high-ranking FBI official with obstructing justice in the Ruby Ridge case by destroying an internal critique of the deadly Idaho siege.
JABAL SAKAJ, Afghanistan - After a decade of battles against the Soviet army and another seven years of factional fighting, war has come to define existence in Afghanistan.

TAMPA - What has happened in Tampa, a crime-afflicted city in a politically critical state, helps explain how crime is playing all over the country as the presidential campaign moves into its final leg.
WASHINGTON - Prince George's County Council endorsed a plan to pour $63 million into education, public safety and other services if voters remove a cap on the property tax rate next month.
MEXICO CITY - President Ernesto Zedillo says he believes drug smuggling is the biggest threat to Mexico's national security.
